champion: Thyroid follicular carcinoma with bone metastasis
ordered_diagnoses: Thyroid follicular carcinoma with bone metastasis

facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s presented with swelling of the manubrium
12 years after resection of a large left substernal thyroid lobe through a midline sternotomy approach
The swelling was slightly tender and had increased in size markedly over the month prior to presentation
Swelling noted over the manubrium, which was slightly tender
CT Image Description: Shows a lytic lesion replacing the manubrium measuring 2.7 × 4.4 × 5.8 cm
and residual right goiter
The posterior aspect is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Revealed follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and the manubrial lesion
Hematoxylin-eosin stained specimens showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae
Medical history includes previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter 12 years ago

concepts.preferred_label: Thyroid follicular carcinoma with bone metastasis
concepts.why: The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae, as shown in the CT image and pathological examination, suggests thyroid follicular carcinoma with bone metastasis.
The patient's medical history includes previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter, and the CT image shows residual right goiter.
The patient presented with swelling of the manubrium, which was slightly tender and had increased in size markedly over the month prior to presentation, suggesting postoperative swelling.
The CT image shows a lytic lesion replacing the manubrium, which could be a primary or metastatic bone lesion.
The posterior aspect of the lytic lesion is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein, suggesting potential vascular compression.
The presence of thyroid follicles in the manubrial lesion, as shown in the fine-needle aspiration and pathological examination, suggests metastatic thyroid cancer.
The patient's medical history includes previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter.
The patient had a previous midline sternotomy approach for substernal left hemithyroidectomy, which would have resulted in a surgical scar.

rationales.F01: Swelling of the manubrium is a non-specific finding that could be related to various conditions.
rationales.F02: History of thyroid surgery increases the likelihood of thyroid-related conditions.
rationales.F05: Lytic lesion replacing the manubrium is a strong indicator of bone metastasis or primary bone tumor.
rationales.F08: Presence of follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and manubrial lesion suggests a thyroid origin.
rationales.F09: Infiltration of thyroid follicles into bone trabeculae is a characteristic feature of thyroid cancer with bone metastasis.
